He later applied those capabilities to rural commerce and social programmes.

long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in a village near Suqian in Jiangsu, Liu Qiangdong reached Renmin University after neighbours contributed money and eggs for his journey to Beijing. He studied sociology and later opened an electronics counter in Zhongguancun. That counter became JD.com after he moved the retail business online.

Known internationally as Richard Liu, he set JD apart by selling goods directly and investing in its own warehousing and delivery network. The logistics decision gave the e-commerce group greater control over product quality and service, while creating a supply-chain business in its own right. Liu later used the same retail and distribution capabilities to support rural producers, linking his business model back to the communities that shaped his early life.
